[b]OPERATION: FIREFALL3rd Paratrooper Division - Combat Log (Classified)Location: Western Ridge, Sal-Baliz TerritoryTimestamp: H+2 hours after drop
[/b]
The cargo bay was filled with tension and the steady roar of turbines. Sweat dripped down the side of my helmet as I glanced at Sergeant Kael across from me. He was checking his harness for the third time.

You ready for this? I asked, shouting over the engine noise.

He gave a tight nod. You ever ready to jump into hell?

Private Dorn, fresh out of academy, piped up. Heard the last unit got torn apart near the ridge.

Yeah, Kael muttered, tightening his grip on the strap, and were here to finish what they started.

The red light above us snapped green.

GO! GO! GO! the jumpmaster bellowed.

We surged forward. The bay doors opened to the shriek of wind and the shrill cry of anti-air fire. Below, the Western Ridge burned orange and black, Sal-Baliz tracers crisscrossing the sky like angry wasps. Two transports in our formation exploded midair, their debris raining past us as we leapt into the chaos.

My chute deployed a heartbeat before I hit the slope. I rolled through smoke and grit, rifle already raised. All around me, troopers were dropping fast, some not even making it to the ground in one piece. The enemy had anti-air emplacements dialed inbut we came down hard anyway.

Within seconds, I was in the dirt beside Kael, bullets snapping overhead. "Rally at the boulder cluster!" he shouted. We regrouped with three other survivors, just in time to take cover from a mortar round that vaporized half a tree.

For the next hour, it was hell. We fought for every meter. Sal-Baliz fighters were dug in, firing from caves, trenches, and shattered ruins. Sgt. Malken went down beside me, chest full of shrapnel. Dorn caught a bullet through the leg but kept shooting, propped against a rock.

Eventually, fireteam Echo breached a forward bunker, silencing one of the AA positions. That was our turning point. We pressed hard, pushing through the line with grenades, bayonets, and raw fury. Tracer rounds lit the sky behind us as the rear guard finally secured the drop zone.

By noon, the ridge was ours. Bodies lined the slope. Smoke still poured from wrecked bunkers. But we held it.

Corporal Jasso found a collapsed gun nest and rammed a flagpole into the dirt, wrapping it with his busted comms cable. "Let em see it," he said. "Let em know we're still breathing."

The engineers dropped in last, escorted by a handful of gunships. No tanks yet. No heavy support. Just prefab shelters, field generators, and a couple of auto-turrets. We set up a rough perimeter using scrap metal and sandbags. The medics turned an old munitions shed into a triage post. We had wounded stacked two-deep inside.

We didnt sleep. We dug. We patrolled. We patched each other up. The camp was basicrough earth, buzzing drones overhead, boiling coffee on a camp stove built from a bent fuel canister. We were still bleeding. But we were standing.

They thought wed break on impact.

But the 3rd Paratrooper Division doesn't break.

We land. We fight. We build.

And we hold.

Sal-Baliz just learned that the hard way.

Were not going anywhere.

[nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] [nation]United Hydronia[/nation]
